newsitem.title: THAILAND: Heroin suspect seeks early extradition to U.S.
newsitem.headline: Heroin suspect seeks early extradition to U.S.

text.p: A drugs suspect accused of masterminding the biggest heroin haul in U.S. history asked a Thai criminal court on Monday to speed up judicial proceeding for his extradition to the United States.
Li Yung Chung told the court in Bangkok he gave up his legal right to contest a U.S. request for Thailand to extradite him to face charges in the United States.

"I would like to apologise to the court and Thailand for the damage that I have done to the court and the Thai people. I am prepared to fight (my court case) in America and would like to ask the court to extradite me as soon as possible," he told the court.

The Burmese government handed over Li, alias Phongsak Rogianasakul, to Thailand on Saturday. He is the main suspect in a drug haul worth up to $122 million in Hayward, California, in 1991, but fled to Burma after jumping bail in Thailand in March while awaiting a court decision on his extradition to the U.S.
Li, an ethnic Chinese with a Thai identity card, was indicted by a New York court in May 1996 in connection with the 486 kg (nearly 1,070 pound) heroin haul.

The Burmese military government denied sheltering Li. It said on Saturday it regarded total eradication of narcotic drugs as a national task and its decision to hand over Li to Thailand was aimed at boosting the region's fight against drug trafficking.
